newsitem.title: DENMARK: Stable Danish bonds seen shadowing Germany.
newsitem.headline: Stable Danish bonds seen shadowing Germany.

text.p: Danish bond prices remained largely static on Thursday, with dealers expecting the market to continue shadowing Germany within a narrow range.
"Denmark is following Germany and I see no reason why this should not continue. The benchmark will trade within the 107.60-85 range all day," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was unchanged from the opening at 107.72, yielding 6.84 percent in turnover of 1.6 billion crowns while its December future fell 0.20 point to 107.06 with 102 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.15 point to 85.10.
The crown traded at 3.8348 per mark at 1010 gmt, down from around 3.8333 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 84 basis points from the start of trade.
